description: OSS files and CI additions. All new files, no changes to existing source code. Independent of all other FEATs except it should be done last so the README can accurately describe the architecture that was built. Creates LICENSE, README.md, docs/self-hosting.md, docs/deployment.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, .github/pull_request_template.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md, and adds the docker CI job to .github/workflows/ci.yml.
steps: Create LICENSE with MIT license text. Year: 2025. Author: 'Notification Service Contributors'.

Create README.md. Sections in order: (1) badge row — CI (linking to .github/workflows/ci.yml), MIT license badge, Docker badge; (2) one-line description; (3) ## Architecture with a Mermaid diagram showing: Client -> API (FastAPI) -> PostgreSQL; API -> Redis (Celery queue); Redis -> Worker (Celery) -> Email Provider / SMS Provider / Webhook; (4) ## Quickstart with three code blocks: `git clone ...`, `python scripts/generate_env.py`, `docker compose up -d`; (5) ## Features bullet list; (6) ## Configuration table with columns Env Var | Default | Description, one row per config.py field using the full table from the plan findings; (7) ## API Quick Reference table with columns Method | Path | Description; (8) ## Development section with manual steps for running backend and frontend locally; (9) ## Contributing link to CONTRIBUTING.md; (10) ## License MIT.

Create docs/ directory if not already present. Create docs/self-hosting.md. Sections: Prerequisites (Docker 24+, Docker Compose v2+), Quick start (5 steps: clone, generate_env.py, review .env, docker compose up -d, visit http://localhost), Service descriptions table (db/redis/migrate/api/worker/web), Running migrations manually, Enabling the scheduler (ENABLE_BEAT=true on the worker service), Backup and restore (docker exec for pg_dump), Upgrading (docker compose pull, docker compose up -d).

Create docs/deployment.md. Sections: Environment variables reference (full table), Scaling API workers (uvicorn --workers or multiple api container replicas), Scaling Celery workers (run multiple worker containers — they share the Redis queue), External managed Postgres (just change DATABASE_URL), External managed Redis (just change REDIS_URL), Reverse proxy (nginx config snippet for SSL termination, setting TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT=1), Rate limiting with Redis (RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_URI=redis://...), TLS/HTTPS (certbot or Cloudflare).

Create CONTRIBUTING.md. Sections: ## Development setup (backend: pip install -r requirements.txt, alembic upgrade head, uvicorn app.main:app --reload; frontend: npm ci, npm run dev), ## Running Tests (`cd backend && pytest -q`), ## Running the Linter (`cd frontend && npm run lint`), ## Commit style (Conventional Commits: feat/fix/docs/chore/refactor/test), ## Pull request process, ## Code of conduct (be respectful).

Create SECURITY.md. Sections: ## Supported versions (latest main branch), ## Reporting a vulnerability (open a GitHub security advisory or email placeholder), ## What we consider a security issue (auth bypass, data exposure, SSRF, injection), ## Response timeline (acknowledge within 48h, patch within 14 days for critical), ## Credits.

Create .github/pull_request_template.md with sections: ## Description, ## Type of change (checkboxes: bug fix, new feature, refactor, docs, chore), ## How has this been tested?, ## Checklist (checkboxes: tests pass, lint passes, docs updated if needed, no secrets committed).

Create .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md with YAML front-matter: name: Bug report, about: Create a report to help us improve, labels: bug. Body template sections: Describe the bug, To Reproduce, Expected behavior, Environment.

Create .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md with YAML front-matter: name: Feature request, about: Suggest an idea, labels: enhancement. Body template sections: Is your feature request related to a problem?, Describe the solution you'd like, Alternatives considered.

Read .github/workflows/ci.yml before editing it. Append a new 'docker' job after the existing 'frontend' job. The job has steps: (1) actions/checkout@v4, (2) 'Validate docker-compose config' running 'docker compose config --quiet', (3) 'Build backend image' running 'docker compose build api', (4) 'Build frontend image' running 'docker compose build web'. The job does NOT start any containers.
acceptance_criteria: README.md exists and contains a Mermaid code block and ## Quickstart section
CONTRIBUTING.md exists and contains ## Running Tests
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md and feature_request.md both exist with valid YAML front-matter
.github/workflows/ci.yml contains a 'docker' job with docker compose build steps
cd frontend && npm run build exits 0 (no regressions from any accidental edits)
